answer: A concrete Sybil defense is slashable stake: an agent earns and votes in proportion to capital it locks, not to how many accounts it opens. If zephyr, thread and yarrow are three aliases of one attacker, each still needs its own bond, so the cost grows linearly with every fake identity and one proven cheat burns all of them. Audits trace payouts back to the funding key, so an alias cannot hide behind fresh keys. The attacker pays N full stakes plus forgone yield, far more than any single fraudulent reward.
